2026-12-21.title: 21 December · Advent Weekday (O Dayspring)
readings: Look, my beloved comes, leaping upon the mountains
Exult, you just, in the Lord! Sing to him a new song
2026-12-21.alt: O Antiphon: O Oriens (O Dayspring). Optional memorial: St Peter Canisius, priest and doctor.
2026-12-21.verse: And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
theo: Today's O Antiphon: “O Dayspring, splendour of eternal light and sun of justice: come and enlighten those who dwell in darkness and the shadow of death.” On the shortest days of the year in the northern hemisphere, the Church sings of the Sun that rises from on high. The Song of Songs gives the voice of the bride: “The voice of my beloved! Look, he comes, leaping upon the mountains.”

Mary, having said yes, does not stay at home. She “set out and went with haste” to the hill country to visit Elizabeth. At her greeting, John leaps in his mother's womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, cries out: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb… And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” The first person to call Jesus “Lord” in Luke's Gospel is an unborn child's mother, and the first to rejoice at his presence is an unborn child. Elizabeth's last word praises Mary's faith: “Blessed is she who believed.”
outline: Ask: whom will you visit before Christmas?
Point 3 · Blessed is she who believed
The unborn John rejoices; Elizabeth blesses Mary's faith.
live: Visit an elderly relative or a pregnant mother before Christmas.
Pray the Hail Mary for unborn children and their mothers.
2026-12-21.prayer: O Dayspring, splendour of eternal light and sun of justice, come and enlighten those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death. Like Mary, let me hasten to serve, and let me be blessed in believing your word. Amen.
altar: At Mass Christ comes to us hidden, as he came to Elizabeth's house in Mary's womb. After Communion we carry him into our homes.

quick: The Beloved comes leaping over the mountains.

2026-12-21.question: Do I believe God will fulfil what he has promised me?

family.explain: Mary hurried to visit Elizabeth. Baby John jumped for joy because Jesus was near.

family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we visit this Christmas?”

pm.open: O Dayspring, sun of justice, come and enlighten those who dwell in darkness. Lord Jesus, as we gather, fill us with the joy of the Visitation. Amen.
share: Mary went with haste (Luke 1:39). Whom should I visit before Christmas?
Elizabeth said: blessed is she who believed (Luke 1:45). Which of God's promises do I find hard to believe?
Where in my life do I need the Dayspring to shine?
pm.resp: Come, O Dayspring, and enlighten us.
interc: For the Church, that she may carry Christ with joy to all people.
For pregnant mothers and their babies.
For the elderly and lonely, that they may be visited this Christmas.
For those in darkness and the shadow of death.
For our group, that we may believe God's promises.
pm.close: Lord God, Mary carried your Son to Elizabeth and filled her home with joy. Make us bearers of Christ, and let the Dayspring from on high shine on all in darkness. Amen.

illus: Every Christmas week a group of young people from a parish in Kozhikode visit the old age home nearby with songs and sweets. One elderly woman told them: “When you come, it is as if Mary came with the Child.”

homily: Dear friends, today's O Antiphon prays: O Dayspring, splendour of eternal light and sun of justice: come and enlighten those who dwell in darkness and the shadow of death.

The Song of Songs sings of love: the voice of my beloved! Look, he comes, leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away; for now the winter is past (Song of Songs 2:8, 10–11). The Church reads it in Advent as God coming to his people with the eagerness of love.

In the Gospel Mary sets out and goes with haste to the hill country, to the house of Zechariah, and greets Elizabeth. When Elizabeth hears Mary's greeting, the child leaps in her womb, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit. She exclaims: blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb! And blessed is she who believed (Luke 1:39–45).

Mary carries Jesus hidden within her, and wherever she goes, joy follows. John the Baptist leaps for joy even before birth. Elizabeth is filled with the Spirit. The Visitation is the first Christmas in a way: Christ arrives at a home, and the home is transformed.
We too carry Christ, especially after Holy Communion. When we visit others with love, Christ comes with us. A visit to a sick neighbour, a lonely grandparent, a family in grief, can be a Visitation.

Elizabeth praises Mary above all for her faith: blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfilment of what was spoken to her by the Lord (Luke 1:45). This Christmas, let us believe God's promises, and carry Christ with haste to someone who needs his joy. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary visited her cousin and brought Jesus with her. When you visit someone with love, you bring Jesus too!

sub: The unborn child recognises his Lord.
Elizabeth is filled with the Spirit.
Every life is precious from the womb.
q: Listen to me, O coastlands, pay attention, you peoples from far away! The LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.

When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and exclaimed with a loud cry, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.”
points.apply: Pray for unborn children and their mothers.

sub: Abraham believed and was reckoned righteous.
Faith is the root of Mary's greatness.
q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.

And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me? For as soon as I heard the sound of your greeting, the child in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
points.apply: Renew your trust in one promise of God.

concl: Christ comes, and the little ones leap for joy.
